headline: Approved moving $210,000 and $209,302 in school capital funds; overrode mayor's veto of Boston Avenue zoning.
summary: Moved school capital funds for intercom systems, Brooks turf, and other repairs. Overrode the mayor's veto of the Boston Avenue zoning amendment, after a motion to require special permits for student housing in BA3 failed. Tabled the McCormick Avenue parcel sale and the FY27 supplemental appropriation, and referred a PILOT framework to committee.
decisions: Approved Papers 26-168, 26-176, and 26-177, resolutions inviting residents to events, 7-0 voice vote.
Approved the records of the September 29, 2026 meeting, 7-0 voice vote.
Approved the Committee of the Whole report from September 30, 2026, 7-0 voice vote.
Approved sending three questions, plus one added question, to the Administration on fire department matters, 7-0 roll call.
Approved moving $210,000 and $209,302 in school capital funds to new projects, 7-0 roll call.
Referred the PILOT and Community Benefits framework resolution to the Committee of the Whole, 7-0 voice vote.
Approved asking the Mayor to remove untrue information about the Boston Avenue zoning vote from the city website, 7-0 voice vote.
Denied motion to require special permits for purpose built student housing in BA3, failing 3-4 on roll call.
Approved overriding the mayor's veto of Boston Avenue zoning and ordaining the BANCD, 7-0 roll call.
Tabled the Law Department appropriations response, 7-0 voice vote.
Tabled the request for an update on the City Charter, 7-0 voice vote.
Tabled the order to transfer and sell McCormick Avenue parcels, 7-0 voice vote.
Tabled the Police Chief search funding request, 7-0 voice vote.
Tabled the FY2027 supplemental appropriation, 7-0 voice vote.

Medford City Council 
Medford, Massachusetts 
  
The Seventeenth Regular Meeting, October 13, 2026 
 
This meeting took place in the City Council Chamber, 2nd Floor, Medford City Hall, 85 George 
P. Hassett Drive, Medford, MA and via Zoom. 
 
CALL TO ORDER 
 
President Zac Bears called the Seventeenth Regular Meeting of the Medford City Council to 
order in the Council Chambers and via Zoom. 
 
ROLL CALL 
 
Present: President Bears; Vice President Lazzaro; Councilor Callahan; Councilor Leming; 
Councilor Mullane; Councilor Scarpelli; Councilor Tseng. Seven members were present and no 
members were absent. Inside the Rail: City Clerk Laurel Siegel. 
 
SALUTE TO THE FLAG 
 
ANNOUNCEMENTS, ACCOLADES, REMEMBRANCES, REPORTS, and RECORDS 
 
26-168 - Resolution to Invite Residents to Ward 5 Neighborhood Meeting on October 20th 
Offered by Liz Mullane, City Councilor 
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we invite the residents of Ward 5 to attend the 
Ward 5 Neighborhood Meeting on October 20th at 7PM at the Missituk Elementary School. This 
meeting will be hosted by Councilor Callahan and Councilor Tseng, and residents are welcome 
to attend and discuss improvements they would like to see in their neighborhood. 
 
For more information and for a Zoom link when it is available, please visit the City Council 
Agenda Portal. 
 
26-176 - Resolution to Invite Residents to the Harvest Your Energy Festival on October 
17th 
Offered by Isaac Bears, Council President 
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we invite residents to attend the Harvest Your 
Energy Festival on Saturday, October 17th from 12:00 to 3:00 pm at Riverbend Park. 
 
For more details about the event visit https://medfordenergy.org/gogreen/harvest-your-energy-
festival/ 
 
26-177 - Resolution to Invite Residents to Sarah Bradlee Fulton Day on October 17th 
Offered by Isaac Bears, Council President 
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we invite residents to attend Sarah Bradlee 
Fulton Day on Saturday, October 17th from 10:00 am to 12:00 pm at the Salem Street Burying 
Ground 
 
For more details about the event please visit the City of Medford Events Calendar.

26-142C - City Council Response to Paper 26-142 
(Fire Chief Evans and Funding for City Solicitor) 
Offered by the City Council 
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we request that Fire Chief Evans appear before 
the Council at the October 13th meeting to answer questions. 
 
Be it Further Resolved that we request an answer from the Mayor regarding whether if the full 
year of the City Solicitor’s salary were to be funded by the Council, would the Mayor post that 
Job and hire a Solicitor or would she use those funds for other outside counsel. 
 
Addressing the Council: 
Jeremiah O’Brien, President, Medford Firefighters Local 1032 
Brian Honeycutt, Secretary for the Union 
Bob Jones, Treasurer for the Union 
 
Motion by Councilor Scarpelli to send the following questions to the Administration, seconded 
by Councilor Tseng: 
• Do we have an understanding for the education credits and payments to our firefighters 
under their contract? 
• For the two suits that have been settled, why haven’t those two firefighters been put back on 
duty? 
• How many Level 1 grievances has the Fire Chief dealt with without further escalation? 
 
Motion amended by Councilor Tseng to add the following additional question, seconded by 
Councilor Scarpelli: 
• Is the Administration agreeing to do an outside audit and review with a public report on the 
legal practices of the City?

26-178 - Resolution to Discuss a PILOT and Community Benefits Framework for Medford 
Offered by Isaac Bears, Council President, Justin Tseng, City Councilor 
 
WHEREAS, the Medford City Council has previously sought to establish a more transparent and 
representative framework for Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT), including through Papers 20-
021 and 20-053, which resulted in the preparation of a draft PILOT Commission ordinance, and 
the Council's 2024–2025 Governing Agenda subsequently contemplated a Community Benefits 
Agreement Ordinance providing for community participation in negotiations with major 
development projects and nonprofit institutions; and  
 
WHEREAS, Medford's last written PILOT agreement with Tufts University expired in 2018, the 
subsequent arrangement was not memorialized in a publicly available written agreement, and 
Medford currently lacks a permanent, publicly established process through which residents and 
the City Council can participate in defining and negotiating PILOT contributions and community 
benefits; and  
 
WHEREAS, large nonprofit institutions and major development projects can have significant and 
lasting impacts on Medford's neighborhoods, housing, infrastructure, public services, and 
finances, and the City would benefit from a transparent and consistent framework for community 
participation, institutional dialogue, negotiated community benefits, and public accountability; 
 
BE IT RESOLVED, that the Medford City Council discuss the development of a comprehensive 
PILOT and Community Benefits framework, including revisiting and updating the previously 
drafted PILOT Commission

26-179 - Resolution to Request an Update from the Mayor Regarding the City Charter 
Offered by Isaac Bears, Council President and Justin Tseng, City Councilor 
 
Whereas, the voters of the City of Medford approved a new City Charter at the last municipal 
election on November 4th, 2025; and 
 
Whereas, members of the City Council and School Committee met with the Mayor and 
representatives of the City Administration several times this year regarding City Charter 
implementation; and 
 
Whereas, the City Administration has not provided a formal response to the City Council and 
School Committee regarding City Charter Implementation; and 
 
Whereas, the City Clerk has not received any communication regarding the City Charter, a copy 
of the finalized language, and how it should be codified in the City's Municode; and 
 
Whereas, the City Council and City Clerk are not aware whether the state has been informed 
regarding the City Charter; now, therefore: 
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we urgently request that the City Administration 
submit the City Charter and the certification from the Department of Elections to the City Clerk 
to be codified in Municode.  
 
Be it Further Resolved that we urgently request that the City Administration meet with the City 
Council and School Committee to finalize an implementation plan for the City Charter.  
 
Be it Further Resolved that the City Administration provide an update on the submission of the 
City Charter to all relevant state agencies. 
 
Motion by Councilor Scarpelli to table, seconded by Councilor Tseng. Approved on a Voice 
Vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed. 
 
26-181 - Order to Transfer and Authorize the Sale of McCormick Avenue Parcels 
Offered by George Scarpelli, City Councilor, and Isaac Bears, Council President 
 
Whereas, the City is the owner of two parcels of land located on McCormack Avenue, each 
containing 3,600 square feet, more or less, identified as the Assessors’ as Parcels F-13/37 and 
F-13/38, and described in Certificate of Title No. 166463 filed with the Middlesex South Registry 
District of the Land Court (together, the “City Property”); 
 
Whereas, the City Property has been vacant and unused since the City acquired the City 
Property in 1950 pursuant a tax taking, and is surplus to the needs of the City; 
 
Whereas, there is an urgent need to promote and develop affordable housing in the City of 
Medford and the region; 
 
Whereas, the sale of the City Property will benefit the City by putting the City Property to 
productive and tax-generating uses; and 
 
Whereas, the proceeds of said sale may be used by the City for the purpose of promoting 
affordable housing; and 
 
Whereas, now that the Affordable Housing Trust has been operating for over a year and the 
Council has reviewed the AHT annual action plan since the vote of the Council not to approve a
8 
 
similar order in April 2025. 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDERED BY THE MEDFORD CITY COUNCIL: 
 
1. That the City Council hereby declares that the City Property is surplus to the needs of the City 
and available for disposition; and 
2. That the City Council hereby transfers the care, custody and control of the City Property from 
the tax custodian for tax title purposes to the Mayor for general municipal purposes and/or for 
the purpose of disposition on such terms and conditions as is in the best interests of the City; 
and 
3. That the Mayor be authorized to convey the City’s right, title and interest in said City Property, 
provided that said sale is in compliance with the provisions of General Laws Chapter 30B, the 
Uniform Procurement Act, and to take any and all other action as may be necessary or 
appropriate to accomplish said disposition; and 
4. That this order shall take effect upon passage. 
 
Motion by Councilor Scarpelli to table, seconded by Councilor Tseng. Approved on a Voice
